context: Implement structure/reference checks, provenance/freshness validation, source-cursor comparison, summary-to-rollout traceability, index-to-topic consistency, sensitivity scanning, duplicate detection, project/root normalization, stale-path detection, and token budgets. Add the twelve adversarial scenarios from the audit with expected retrieval, rejected memories, required live verification, answer properties, failure conditions, and a 0-2 rubric across recall, rejection, provenance, freshness, completion, isolation, privacy, and correctness. Add mutation tests for every guard.
description: Build a deterministic, versioned evaluation harness in the repository selected by the phase-0 decision. Baseline from the 2026-07-27 audit: Codex 43 files / 6,444 lines / 534,897 bytes (~133,724 approximate tokens), globally injected summary 103 lines / 9,437 bytes (~2,359 tokens), 37 valid rollout and source-session references, four summaries with materially later source activity, at least 87 duplicated long lines / 100 extra occurrences, 75 pool-path lines and 13 temporary-path lines; Claude 39 files / 1,563 lines / 92,960 bytes (~23,240 tokens), BenchBox startup index ~2,001 tokens, one orphan topic, and five project-memory roots among eleven encoded project-state directories. Neither system had freshness/expiry fields. A targeted Markdown scan found zero high-confidence token/JWT/key/private-key strings but three files with private operational markers. Behavioral precision, recall, latency, and tool-call baselines were intentionally not run against live homes. The harness must operate on checksummed fixture copies and include baseline, treatment, and minimal/disabled-memory arms.

anti_patterns.instead: record rule IDs, file counts, and redacted locations only
anti_patterns.why: a privacy evaluator must not become a new disclosure surface

anti_patterns.dont: run baseline behavioral sessions against the live Codex or Claude homes
anti_patterns.instead: use isolated CODEX_HOME and Claude autoMemoryDirectory fixtures with generation disabled
anti_patterns.why: the evaluation would mutate the system being measured

anti_patterns.dont: treat exact duplicate-line counts as semantic duplicate detection
anti_patterns.instead: report exact and semantic similarity metrics separately
anti_patterns.why: paraphrased duplication and qualification loss are the higher-risk cases

preserves.behavior: Baseline and treatment remain independently reproducible and checksummed
Evaluation does not contribute its own sessions to future memory
Fixture generation never copies or reports secret values or sensitive transcript text

verifications.expected: all structural and mutation tests pass
